extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, communications managers, and marketers writing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for drafting and distributing press releases in 2024, covering format, length, SEO, multimedia, and distribution tactics targeted at journalists and online discovery. Aimed at modern PR/communications teams adapting to mobile, social, and AI-driven news workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-format (text + assets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-format (text + assets)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern press releases should include both written copy and supporting assets (photos, video, infographics) rather than text-only releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO optimization for Google and Google News
rubrics_metrics.description: SEO-optimized for both Google and Google News
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write releases to be discoverable by search engines and news aggregators; include keywords and consider News-specific factors so both Google Search and Google News can index the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-first distribution timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Social-first in distribution timing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time distribution to maximize social engagement and visibility; prioritize channels and schedules that work well for social platforms and journalists who source stories from social feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designed to be excerpted
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to be excerpted, not republished verbatim
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write copy that can be easily excerpted by journalists and publishers—short, crisp lead that can serve as an excerpt rather than expecting full republishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimized for AI summarization
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimized for AI summarization (LLMs scrape press releases)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure and language should be friendly to LLMs and automated summarizers which may scrape releases for summaries; front-load important facts and make structure clear for better AI-generated excerpts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target length: 300–400 words
rubrics_metrics.description: 300-400 words is the new sweet spot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for ~300–400 words (down from the 600–800 word standard of the 2010s) to reflect shorter journalist attention windows and mobile reading behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile-first — most reads happen on phone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mobile-friendly paragraphing, short sentences, and formatting that reads well on phones; consider how headlines, subheads, and assets appear on small screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-load primary keyword in headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary keyword in headline (front-loaded)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the primary keyword at or near the start of the headline to improve SEO and make topic immediately clear for readers and scrapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary keywords in subhead
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary keywords in subhead
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subheads to include secondary or supporting keywords to reinforce SEO without stuffing the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include 1–2 backlinks to landing pages
rubrics_metrics.description: 1-2 backlinks to landing pages, not homepage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit outbound links to one or two, pointing to relevant landing pages (product pages, campaign pages) rather than the site homepage; avoid excessive linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use descriptive anchor text
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor text should be descriptive, not "click here"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer meaningful, keyword-rich anchor text that explains the linked content, improving usability and SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Schema.org NewsArticle markup when self-hosted
rubrics_metrics.description: Schema.org NewsArticle markup if posting on own site
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publishing the press release on your own domain, include NewsArticle schema to help search engines and news aggregators understand and surface the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum one high-res photo
rubrics_metrics.description: One high-res photo MINIMUM (1200x630 for social)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one downloadable high-resolution image sized for social sharing (recommended 1200x630) to ensure visual assets display properly on platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional short b-roll video
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: short b-roll video (under 60 seconds)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief video clips (<60s) when possible to increase pick-up and social sharing; keep videos short and easily embeddable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional shareable infographic
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: shareable infographic with social-media dimensions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide infographics sized for social platforms to encourage shares and visual storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets must be downloadable without registration
rubrics_metrics.description: All assets should be downloadable without registration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure journalists and aggregators can access and download photos, videos, and files without needing to log in or register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't rely only on wire services
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire services losing influence (Cision/PRN/BW now scraped by AI for summaries)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a wire-only strategy; wires are increasingly scraped for summaries by AI and may not be sufficient for outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct journalist outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct outreach via Muck Rack, Qwoted, or HARO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement wire distribution with targeted, personalized outreach using journalist databases and platforms to build relationships and increase pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch via Twitter DMs when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch via Twitter DMs to active journalists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use journalists' active social DMs (e.g., Twitter/X) for succinct, timely pitches when appropriate, but keep outreach targeted and personalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LinkedIn newsletters as channel
rubrics_metrics.description: LinkedIn newsletters as alternative channel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider distributing or pitching stories through LinkedIn newsletters as an alternative channel to reach readers and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email pitches for Substack-native journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Substack-native journalists prefer email pitches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When targeting writers who publish on Substack, use email pitches as many prefer that channel over social DMs or wire copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass-blast distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass-blast distribution (gets filtered as spam)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sending mass, untargeted blasts that are likely to be filtered as spam or ignored; prioritize quality, targeted outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always include visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases without visuals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases lacking visuals are less effective—include images or other media to improve pickup and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep 'About Us' boilerplate concise
rubrics_metrics.description: "About Us" boilerplate longer than 75 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the boilerplate to 75 words or fewer to keep background concise and useful to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep quotes short
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes longer than 35 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid long quoted passages; keep quotes under ~35 words to be easily excerpted and to maintain readability.
